Reuters: Standard Chartered’s Crypto Custody Unit Zodia Suffers Security Breach According to Reuters, Standard Chartered’s crypto custody unit Zodia Custody suffered a security breach this week, exposing client and employee data, including names and email addresses. Zodia Custody CEO Richard Clark confirmed the incident in an emailed statement to Reuters, saying the breach was discovered on November 23. It remains unclear whether any crypto assets held in custody were affected. — link

JPMorgan: Strategy’s mNAV Hits Record Low of 0.88x, Below Previous Low in Late June JPMorgan analysts said Strategy’s valuation relative to its bitcoin holdings has fallen to a record low of around 0.88x, below its previous low in late June, signaling capitulation in the bitcoin market. BlackRock’s spot bitcoin ETF (IBIT) continued to see outflows despite a brief recovery in bitcoin’s price, with the pace of outflows appearing to exceed that observed from early May to late June. The analysts previously said retail investors likely drove much of the recent crypto ETF outflows and may have shifted funds into equity ETFs. They also noted that the widening gap between bitcoin’s market price and their estimated production cost of around $86,000 was likely increasing pressure on higher-cost miners to sell bitcoin from their reserves. — link

Bitcoin Core Contributor Finds $0.35 Attack Could Link Bitcoin Addresses to Node IPs Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail disclosed on Delving Bitcoin that a long-known privacy weakness in Bitcoin Core’s wallet rebroadcast mechanism could allow attackers to link Bitcoin addresses to the IP addresses of nodes tracking them for less than $0.35 per attempt. The method achieved a 100% success rate across 30 simulated attributions on a regression test network (regtest), but has not been validated on mainnet. The weakness affects both hot and watch-only wallets, meaning an identified node does not necessarily control the associated funds. Other potentially affected software includes Bitcoin Knots, Sparrow in Bitcoin Core mode, Specter Desktop, Liana and Electrum Personal Server. Disabling wallet broadcasting can mitigate the risk but requires users to broadcast their transactions manually. A proposed code change, PR #36482, remains unreleased and does not eliminate all rebroadcast-related privacy risks. — link

Hong Kong-Based Market Maker Auros, Which Survived the FTX Collapse, Is Gradually Winding Down Operations According to CoinDesk, citing two sources familiar with the matter, Hong Kong-based crypto market maker Auros is gradually winding down operations. The reasons and timeline remain unclear, and the firm has not responded to requests for comment. Founded in 2019, Auros estimated it handled around 4% of global crypto exchange trading volume, according to co-founder and CIO Ben Roth in July 2024. After FTX’s collapse in 2022 left some of its assets trapped, Auros entered court-supervised restructuring in the British Virgin Islands before exiting provisional liquidation in March 2023 following a $17 million funding round led by Vivienne Court, with participation from Bit Digital. Auros later invested in projects including Pyth and Berachain and launched Aurora, an institutional trading portal connecting centralized and decentralized markets, in September 2026. — link
